title: Add a release checklist, tag CI, and the 1.0.0 bump
lead:
Tagging 1.0.0 needs a repeatable, documented procedure and the actual version
bump. This slice is the final gate that turns a green tree into a release.
boundary:
**Not in this slice:** the PyPI account/name setup and trusted-publishing config
(owned by the publish slice); this consumes it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
A one-off manual release is error-prone and unrepeatable. The bump, the tag, and
the automated publish should be a written checklist backed by CI.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `RELEASING.md` (new)
- `pyproject.toml` — bump to `1.0.0`
- `.github/workflows/` — a tag-triggered build/publish workflow
- `CHANGELOG.md` — close the `[1.0.0]` section

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: The packaging test still builds; `check`/`verify` green.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Write `RELEASING.md`: run `check`, `verify`, the full suite; update the
CHANGELOG; bump the version; tag `v1.0.0`; let CI build and publish. Add the
tag-triggered workflow (see the publish slice for the PyPI mechanics). Perform
the bump to 1.0.0 here once the depended-on gates are done.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Following `RELEASING.md` end to end produces a tagged, buildable 1.0.0; CI is
wired to the tag.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit (the tag itself is created by the release procedure, not this slice).
